yaw.selection: median absolute nonzero yaw, training split only

limitations: Four deterministic held-out anchors; not a full benchmark.
No simulator ground truth for alternative controls or beyond cached frame 49.
Counterfactual differences measure sensitivity, not direction correctness.
100 steps exceed the trained 20-step windows; input history remains 16 states.
Zero input is not guaranteed to stop physical momentum.

summary.scope: Four fixed held-out anchors, equal clip weights; aggregate PSNR computed from pooled MSE

findings: Real-latent reconstructions retain scene layout but show blur and repeated patch textures.
Different controls change short-horizon outputs; no matched simulator truth establishes directional correctness.
Predicted-latent outputs progressively lose scene structure; 100-step examples largely become smooth color fields with patch textures.
At horizon 40, pooled PSNR is 21.888 dB for real-latent decoding and 13.082 dB for predicted-latent decoding.
Prediction LPIPS is worse than raw-RGB persistence on the four-anchor average at every measured horizon despite generally better PSNR.
Predictor output normalization keeps latent RMS near one; finite values and stable RMS do not demonstrate semantic stability.
visual_review.recommendation: Investigate autoregressive predictor drift and predicted-versus-real latent mismatch before increasing decoder-only training; any new formal training requires a separate budget decision.
